## Slide 1: What Is a Volcano?

A volcano is an opening in Earth’s surface where hot melted rock, ash, and gases can escape.

The melted rock is called magma when it is underground. When it comes out of the volcano, it is called lava.

Volcanoes can be found on land and under the ocean.

Add a picture: A volcano erupting with lava.

---

## Slide 2: How Volcanoes Form

Volcanoes often form where tectonic plates move.

Tectonic plates are huge pieces of Earth’s crust. When they push together, pull apart, or slide past each other, magma can rise to the surface.

Over time, lava cools and hardens, building up the volcano.

Add a picture: Diagram of tectonic plates and magma.

---

## Slide 3: Types of Volcanoes

There are different types of volcanoes.

Shield volcanoes are wide and gently sloped. They usually have slow lava flows.

Composite volcanoes are tall and steep. They can have powerful eruptions.

Cinder cone volcanoes are smaller and made from ash and rock pieces.

Add a picture: Three volcano shapes side by side.

---

## Slide 4: What Happens During an Eruption?

During an eruption, lava, ash, rocks, and gases can shoot out of a volcano.

Some eruptions are quiet, with lava slowly flowing out.

Other eruptions are explosive and dangerous.

Volcanic ash can cover the sky, damage buildings, and affect breathing.

Add a picture: Volcano eruption with ash cloud.

---

## Slide 5: Famous Volcanoes

Mount Vesuvius in Italy erupted in the year 79 and buried the city of Pompeii.

Mauna Loa in Hawaii is one of the largest volcanoes on Earth.

Mount St. Helens in the United States had a major eruption in 1980.

Volcanoes can be dangerous, but they also create new land and rich soil.
